findings.summary: The restore re-dispatch never refreshes the cleaner result it routes from, so a second RESTORE is routed to the no-op post-approval stub instead of the cleaner that wrote, and the restore round's bytes are attributed to that stub in the change summary.
findings.evidence:
Probe (temporary `it` appended to the `final evaluation and reuse` describe in `src/qa-orchestration-gates.test.ts`, reverted afterwards): the S1/S3 fixture with `clean: cleanPolicyMember`, `stageWrites: false`, and an `evaluator-final` that returns a `FAIL` carrying one `PRESERVATION` / `repair: "RESTORE"` finding on attempts 1 AND 2 and `passingReview` on attempt 3. Command: `npx vitest run src/qa-orchestration-gates.test.ts -t "QA PROBE"` (passed, 34.0s). Output:
  `PROBE cleanerPrompts: 3 stageCalls: [{"stageId":"post-approval-writing"},{"stageId":"post-approval-writing","repair":"RESTORE"}] finalCalls: 3`
  `PROBE last change summary byStage: {"cleaner":["README.md", ...qa artifacts...],"post-approval-writing":["README.md"]}`
The cleaner attempt events show the cleaner did write last before attempt 2 — `["cleaner",3,"PASS","ca73af39...","b303267a..."]` immediately preceding `["final-evaluation",2,"GRADED","b303267a..."]` — yet the second restore went to the stub with `repair: "RESTORE"`.
Root cause is readable in the source: `const cleaner = await dispatchCleanerStage({...})` (src/orchestrator.ts:7162) and `const stageInputTreeId = ...` (src/orchestrator.ts:7250) are computed once and never reassigned, while the restore re-dispatch at src/orchestrator.ts:8042 discards the `CleanerStageResult` it returns. On the next loop iteration `buildWritingStageIds` (src/orchestrator.ts:7898) therefore compares the *new* `currentFinalTreeId` against the *stale* `stageInputTreeId`, appends `POST_APPROVAL_WRITING_STAGE_ID`, and B-01's last-id rule names the stub.
findings.expected: Contract B-01/B-02: `writingStageIds` holds "only the stages that actually changed the tree, in the order they ran", so "a `RESTORE` route whose `stageId` is `CLEANER_STAGE_ID` re-dispatches the cleaner instead of the stub" (B-03) whenever the cleaner is the stage that wrote most recently. Contract B-12: `writeFinalChangeSummary`'s `stages` is "tiled per stage that actually wrote", so "the cleaner's bytes are attributed to the cleaner" and not to the stub.
findings.observed: After one cleaner restore re-dispatch, the cleaner is the only stage that wrote (production's post-approval stage is a no-op, and the fixture's is `stageWrites: false`), but the next attempt's `writingStageIds` is `[cleaner, post-approval-writing]`: the restore is handed to `noopPostApprovalWritingStage` with `repair: "RESTORE"`, which writes nothing, and the change summary attributes the restore round's `README.md` change to `post-approval-writing`. Both are the exact defects this slice exists to remove, reappearing on the second restore.
findings.clearCondition: A run whose final evaluator returns a `RESTORE` on two consecutive attempts, with the cleaner as the only stage that writes, routes both restores to `cleaner`: the injected post-approval writing stage is never called with `repair: "RESTORE"`, and the change summary written for the second attempt attributes the restore round's changed paths to `cleaner` with an empty `post-approval-writing` span. A regression test on the shared `finalEvaluationFixture` covers it.

findings.summary: The `quality-stage-attempt` event for a final-evaluation attempt sets `inputTreeId` to the graded tree rather than to the cited baseline tree, contradicting the locked contract and the acceptance manifest.
findings.evidence: `src/orchestrator.ts:7728` reads `inputTreeId: currentFinalTreeId,` inside `emitFinalAttemptEvent`, with `outputTreeId: currentFinalTreeId` on the following line and a comment defending the equality ("Input and output are the same tree because an evaluation reads"). Confirmed on the stream by the probe of QA-01: every `final-evaluation` line carries the same value in both slots — `["final-evaluation",1,"GRADED","e76c42b3...","e76c42b3..."]`, `["final-evaluation",2,"GRADED","b303267a...","b303267a..."]` — while the cited approved baseline for that run is `ca73af39...` (the accepted tree named as `inputTreeId` of cleaner round 1). No test asserts `inputTreeId` for a final-evaluation attempt: the S1 assertion at `src/qa-orchestration-gates.test.ts` checks `outputTreeId` only, so the deviation is unpinned in either direction.
findings.expected: Contract B-08: "`inputTreeId` = the baseline tree cited, `outputTreeId` = `currentFinalTreeId`". Acceptance manifest B-08 `then`: "the cited baseline tree as inputTreeId, the graded tree as outputTreeId".
findings.observed: `inputTreeId === outputTreeId === currentFinalTreeId` for every final-evaluation attempt, so the event cannot answer which tree the attempt started from — the tree-identity fact PRD D11 asks the family to carry — and the run stream disagrees with the locked behavior text.
findings.clearCondition: A final-evaluation `quality-stage-attempt` line carries the cited approved-baseline tree id as `inputTreeId` and the graded tree id as `outputTreeId`, asserted on the run's own stream (both values, not just `outputTreeId`) in the S1 scenario.

findings.summary: `src/logger.ts` now contains a raw NUL byte, used as the pooling-key separator, which makes git treat the whole file as binary and stop diffing it.
findings.evidence: `git diff --stat 8bbb969..HEAD -- src/logger.ts` reports `src/logger.ts | Bin 33823 -> 41253 bytes` instead of a line diff; the same is true of `git diff --stat main...HEAD`. The byte is new in this slice: `[byte]0` count is 1 in the working file at offset 7336 and 0 in both `main:src/logger.ts` and `8bbb969:src/logger.ts`. `Grep` on the file reports `binary file matches (found "\0" byte around offset 7336)`. The byte sits inside the template literal at `src/logger.ts:210`, which the Read tool renders as `const key = `${attempt.ghIssue} ${attempt.stage}`;` because the NUL is unprintable. The escape `\u0000` would produce the identical key with no NUL byte in the source.
findings.expected: Convention: source files in this repo are text, and every changed line is reviewable in a diff — `readAdvisoryGateOutcomes`, the reader B-09 is modelled on, uses no such separator.
findings.observed: Every future `git diff`, `git log -p`, blame-by-diff and code-review tool reports `src/logger.ts` as a binary blob, so the 8.8KB this slice added to the file — and everything added to it from now on — is unreviewable without `--text`.
findings.clearCondition: `git diff --text=never main...HEAD -- src/logger.ts` renders a textual line diff, and `src/logger.ts` contains no byte equal to 0.

findings.summary: A restore re-dispatch's rounds report the original accepted tree as `inputTreeId`, not the cleaner-committed tree the round actually started from.
findings.evidence: Probe of QA-01: the re-dispatched rounds are journaled as `["cleaner",2,"REVERTED","ca73af39...","791c9b5f..."]` and `["cleaner",3,"PASS","ca73af39...","b303267a..."]`, both naming `ca73af39...` — the same `inputTreeId` cleaner round 1 reported — even though round 1 had already committed `e76c42b3...` and the worktree HEAD carried it when the restore round began. The re-dispatch at `src/orchestrator.ts:8042` reuses the same `CleanerStageInput`, whose accepted tree id is the pre-cleaner tree.
findings.expected: Contract B-07: one event per cleaner round carrying that round's own tree identity, so `inputTreeId === outputTreeId` is the claim "this round changed nothing" (`src/run-events.ts` member doc).
findings.observed: A restore round claims an input tree that no round of it ever read, so the per-round tree chain on the stream is discontinuous and the ROI evidence cannot be walked round by round.
findings.clearCondition: A restore re-dispatch's `quality-stage-attempt` lines name the tree the round actually started from as `inputTreeId` — the previous cleaner round's output — asserted on the run's own stream.
